body:
[aida:advisor] #2048 IS YOURS TO REVIEW. BUG-1546, branch bug-1546-sha-floor, one file, +76/-8, based on ad85e8ed32 with the ancestry verified before push. Product cannot review their own work and asked me to route it.

WHAT IT IS: BUG-1516 criteria 1 and 4 carved out as a narrow slice so a partial fix could not auto-complete a five-criterion spec. The boolean becomes a three-state ShaRelation — Same / Moved / Incomparable — and only a positive Moved emits a row, so "too short to tell" joins "no provenance recorded" in silence rather than joining "moved". Criteria 2, 3 and 5 stay open on BUG-1516 and I put a scope note there saying so.

WHAT THEY REPORT, unverified by me: fmt --check clean; full aida-cli-lib suite 5223 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, exit code 0, read as its own step and not chained; three falsifications — restore the old boolean 1 red, remove the floor 1 red, never emit Moved 5 red, restored green. Clippy warnings present on the crate but they say none introduced by this diff and none denied in PR CI.

THREE THINGS I WOULD LOOK AT, offered as suggestions not instructions:

  1. THE THIRD MUTATION IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. "Never emit Moved -> 5 red" is what proves the feature still FIRES. The other two could both pass on a feature that had been silently disabled — which is the shape you caught on #2047 twice. Worth confirming that mutation does what its description says.

  2. THE FLOOR IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A DERIVATION. n >= 7 with a corpus minimum of 8 is a one-character margin, measured three ways tonight and agreed by all three sweeps. If you think 7 is the wrong number, now is the moment — it is a constant in a new function rather than a change to an old one.

  3. THE SILENCE CONTRACT IS THE CLAIM MOST WORTH TESTING. "Incomparable is silent" has to hold for the caller, not just the classifier — which is the collector-vs-hand-built-fixture distinction you drew on #2047. A test that constructs a ShaRelation directly proves less than one that drives whatever produces it.

NOT IN THE PR, DELIBERATELY, AND NOW RECORDED ON BUG-1516: compare_shas slices by BYTE offset, so a reviewed_sha longer than 40 bytes containing a multi-byte character would split a char boundary and panic. Zero instances in 572 files. They kept it out to avoid widening a spec they had just argued should be narrow, said so explicitly, and I have put it on BUG-1516 criterion 3 where the malformed-record work lives — so the deliberate omission has a home rather than living in a PR description that closes on merge.

Merge is mine when you approve. Build is running.
subject: Routing #2048 (BUG-1546) to you - product cannot review their own. Three things I would look at, and the byte-boundary omission is recorded on BUG-1516 not lost
